Can a moving wormhole mouth send one pulse into Earth's past?

This comparator integrates a smooth, sub-light-speed mouth history and its proper clock in a flat exterior. Change the endpoint separation to see how a target's position changes the route. The default uses the illustrative Earth-center displacement between 6 BCE and 2026 calculated elsewhere in the Book; that date is not a historical identification, and Earth's center is not a safe exit. The finite throat, source stress-energy, and Earth world-tube are not solved here.

Equal mouth-clock readings pair the present moving-mouth event with this earlier event on the stationary target mouth.
The smooth endpoint-motion term is added to this sinusoidal profile; the solver rejects any superluminal samples.
Light-years. Default: illustrative Earth-center target offset. The plotted one-dimensional axis represents the vector's magnitude; orient it toward the selected target in a 3D model.

Mouth worldlines in one exterior frame

Blue: traveling mouth. Gold dashed: stationary target mouth. Position includes the nonzero endpoint offset. The small initial gap $d_0$ is omitted at this light-year scale; the mouths are not allowed to overlap. This is the exterior kinematic history only, not the through-throat path.

Both mouth clocks keep running forward

The moving clock accumulates less proper time because of its motion. At the final event its reading matches the stationary mouth's earlier reading. This equal-clock map shifts a pulse's exit epoch but preserves the order of a pulse sequence.

What this buys the story: under an assumed traversable-throat map, one continuous signal could be aimed at a past target event while the hull and crew stay home. What it does not buy: a reverse-ordered mind-journey, a way to create or move a wormhole mouth, a solved finite null path, or a safe historical witness intercept. The prescribed moving mouth still travels thousands of light-years; if no matter may make that excursion, this comparator does not satisfy the premise.

Target and sighting are separate events. The exit must be placed on the historical target world-tube. Light then follows a future-directed null path to each witness; its travel time determines the sighting date. The 0.202422-ly default is only an Earth-center kinematic benchmark. Replace it with the actual above-surface emitter and witness states before calling the route a Bethlehem reconstruction.
